q: 1. The least count of prismatic compass is
explain: A standard prismatic compass is generally graduated to allow readings to a least count of about 15 minutes of arc.

q: 2. The vertical angle between longitudinal axis of a freely suspended magnetic needle and horizontal line at its pivot, is known
explain: Magnetic dip is the angle that a magnetic needle makes with the horizontal plane due to the Earth's magnetic field lines. It is 0° at the equator and 90° at the poles.

q: 3. The total number of zeroes graduated on a surveyor's compass is
explain: A surveyor's compass, graduated in the quadrantal bearing system, has two zero marks (at the North and South ends), unlike the prismatic compass which has only a single zero (North) on its whole-circle graduated ring.

q: 4. At the equator, the amount of dip is
explain: At the magnetic equator, the earth's magnetic field lines run horizontal, so a freely suspended needle shows zero dip.

q: 5. The graduated ring of a prismatic compass is graduated in
options: any of the system mentioned above
explain: The prismatic compass has its graduated ring marked continuously from 0 deg to 360 deg, i.e., in the whole circle bearing system.

q: 6. The first temporary adjustment of a prismatic compass is centering, levelling, for all
explain: The very first temporary adjustment carried out for a prismatic compass at each station is centering it exactly over the survey station.

q: 7. Which of the following may not cause local attraction on a magnetic needle?
options: loop of a wire carrying electrical current
explain: Wooden pegs, being non-magnetic and non-conducting, do not cause any local attraction on a compass needle, unlike current-carrying wires or steel objects.

q: 8. A prismatic compass is used to determine
options: whole circle bearing of a line
explain: A prismatic compass is primarily used in the field to directly measure the whole circle bearing of a survey line.

q: 9. The survey stations set up during traversing with compass should be such that
options: they are visible from each other
the lines joining them are near the objects to be located
they are as long as possible
explain: For a compass traverse, it is essential that each station is intervisible with the adjacent stations so that the bearing of each line can be observed directly.

q: 10. The magnetic bearing of a line differs for the true bearing by
explain: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing $pm$ Declination. Whether the declination is East or West determines how the two bearings differ.

q: 11. If the whole circle bearing of a line is 120°, its quadrant bearing is
explain: 120° lies in the second quadrant (SE). Quadrant Bearing = $180 - 120 = 60°$. Thus, S 60° E.

q: 12. Reduced bearing of a line is an angle between
options: north line and given line measured clockwise
north line and given line measured anti-clockwise
east or west and the given line
given line and the part of the meridian whether n end or s end, lying adjacent
explain: Reduced Bearing (RB) is measured from either the North or South pole (whichever is closer) toward the East or West.

q: 13. If the whole circle bearing of a line is 270° its reduced bearing is
explain: A bearing of 270° is exactly West. In the Quadrantal system, this is represented as W 90°.

q: 14. In the prismatic compass .............
options: the magnetic needle moves with the box
the line of sight doesn't move with the box
the magnetic needle and graduated circle do not move with the box
explain: In a prismatic compass, the needle and the graduated ring are attached; they remain stationary relative to the magnetic meridian while the box rotates.

q: 15. Local attraction in compass surveying may exist due to .............
options: incorrect leveling of the magnetic needle
loss of magnetism of the needle
friction of the needle at the pivot
presence of magnetic substances near the instrument
explain: Local attraction is caused by external magnetic objects (iron ore, steel structures, power lines) interfering with the Earth's magnetic field.

q: 16. The horizontal angle between true meridian and magnetic meridian at a place is called .............
explain: Magnetic declination is the angle of deviation between the true North and the magnetic North at a specific location.

q: 17. Azimuth (direct angles) is an angle measured in
explain: Azimuth is measured clockwise from the North (or South) meridian.

q: 18. In a quadrantal system, the bearing of a line is measured
options: clockwise or anticlockwise from North/South whichever is nearer...
explain: In the Reduced Bearing (RB) or Quadrantal system, bearings are measured from either North or South towards East or West, whichever is closer, ranging from 0° to 90°.

q: 19. In a whole circle bearing system N25°15'W corresponds to
explain: To convert N 25°15' W to WCB: 360° - 25°15' = 334°45' (since the bearing is in the 4th quadrant).

q: 20. If the fore bearing of a line is 36°15', its back bearing will be
explain: Back Bearing = Fore Bearing ± 180°. Since 36°15' is less than 180°, we add 180°: 36°15' + 180° = 216°15'.

q: 21. If the fore bearing of a line is N26°35'W, its back bearing will be
explain: In the Quadrantal system, the back bearing has the same numerical value but opposite cardinal directions (N becomes S, W becomes E).

q: 22. When the whole circle bearing of two lines AB and AC are 115° and 41° respectively, then the included angle BAC will be
explain: The included angle BAC is the difference between the bearings of the two lines: 115° - 41° = 74°.

q: 23. The horizontal angle between the true meridian and a survey line is called
explain: Azimuth is the horizontal angle measured clockwise from the true north (true meridian) to the survey line.

q: 24. The horizontal angle between the truth meridian and magnetic meridian is known as
explain: Magnetic declination is the horizontal angle by which the magnetic needle deviates from the true north at a specific location.

q: 25. Imaginary line passing through points having equal magnetic declination is termed as
explain: Isogonic lines (isogons) connect points on the earth's surface where the magnetic declination is the same at a given time.

q: 26. Magnetic declination at any place
explain: Magnetic declination is subject to various changes over time, including secular, annual, and diurnal variations.

q: 27. Magnetic bearing of a survey line at any place
options: is always greater than true bearing
explain: Because of annual and secular variations in magnetic declination, the magnetic bearing of a fixed line will change over the months and years.

q: 28. Prismatic compass is considered more accurate than a surveyor's compass, because
options: graduation are in whole circle bearings
explain: The prism allows the surveyor to read the graduated ring while simultaneously sighting the object, leading to higher precision and reduced observation error.

q: 29. If the whole circle bearing of a line is 180°, its reduced bearing is
explain: A WCB of 180° points directly South. In the reduced bearing system, this is simply denoted as 'South' (S).

q: 30. The zero of the graduated circle of prismatic compass is located at
explain: In a prismatic compass, the 0° mark is at the South end so that the reading under the prism (at the observer's end) correctly reflects the magnetic North bearing.

q: 31. The true meridian of a place is the line in which earth's surface in intersected by a plane through
explain: The true meridian is the great circle passing through the geographical North and South poles and the observer's position.

q: 32. True meridian of different places
options: converge from the south pole to the north pole
converge from the north pole to the south pole
converge from the equator to the poles
explain: True meridians are not parallel; they converge at the poles and have their maximum distance apart at the equator.

q: 33. True meridians are generally preferred to magnetic meridians because
options: these change due to change time
explain: Unlike the magnetic meridian, which shifts due to declination changes, the true meridian is fixed and remains constant for any given location.

q: 34. During secular variation of magnetic meridian at different places
explain: Secular variation is a long-term swing (like a pendulum). Both the time it takes (period) and the total degree of swing (range) vary across centuries and locations.

q: 35. Diurnal variation of magnetic declination is
options: less at equator than nearer the poles
explain: Diurnal (daily) variation is generally smaller at the equator and increases as you move toward the magnetic poles.

q: 36. The lines passing through points at which the magnetic declination is equal at a given time are called .............
explain: Isogonic lines connect points of equal magnetic declination. Agonic lines connect points of zero declination.

q: 37. Isogonic lines are the lines having the same .............
explain: Isogonic lines connect points on the earth's surface where the magnetic declination is the same.

q: 38. If whole circle bearing of a line is 120°, its reduced bearing is .............
explain: A bearing of 120° is in the second quadrant (SE). $RB = 180 - 120 = 60$. Thus, S 60° E.

q: 39. The reduced bearing of a line is N 87° W. Its whole bearing is .............
explain: N 87° W is in the fourth quadrant. $WCB = 360 - 87 = 273°$.

q: 40. When the magnetic bearing of the sun at noon is 185° 20', the magnetic declination will be .............
explain: At noon, the sun is at True South (180°). If the magnetic bearing is 185° 20', the magnetic meridian is to the West of True North. $Declination = 180° - 185° 20' = -5° 20'$, or 5° 20' W.

q: 41. When the magnetic declination is 5° 20' east, the magnetic bearing of the sun at noon will be .............
explain: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing + Declination (East is positive). At noon, True Bearing = 180°. $180° = MB + 5° 20'$. $MB = 174° 40'$.

q: 42. The magnetic bearing of a lines is 55° 30' and the magnetic declination is 4° 30' west. The true bearing of a line will be .............
explain: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing - Declination (West is negative). $TB = 55° 30' - 4° 30' = 51° 00'$.

q: 43. The variation of magnetic declination within a day is called .............
explain: Diurnal variation refers to the systematic changes in magnetic declination that occur over a 24-hour period, typically influenced by the sun's position.
